gap: No result ChatGPT got states Apple's own rule for MagSafe charging: 'Don't place credit cards, security badges, passports, or key fobs between your iPhone and MagSafe Charger' (the stated risk is damage to magnetic strips or RFID chips), and 'If you have a case that holds any of these sensitive items, remove them before charging'. So no wallet case, not even a MagSafe one, is meant to be charged wirelessly with cards in it.
standout_why: I opened Macworld's iPhone 17 cases page (cited in one chat). In the part I could read it names no wallet case and says nothing about charging with cards. Our own dealectric.com page says MagSafe wallets must come off to charge and cites Apple only on magnetic-stripe cards versus the magnets. It also says 'chip bank cards are fine', which ignores Apple's separate RFID-chip warning for the charger, and it leaves the Mujjo row as 'with cards in, not checked'. The ChatGPT answers say only that the Smartish has no wireless charging and that you should take the Side Hustle wallet off to charge. None of them says a one-piece card-pocket case (Mujjo, Bellroy 3 Card, Vena vCommuteX) needs its cards taken out before charging. I could not open Good Housekeeping, Wirecutter (direct or through the proxy URL), Best Products or WIRED; they refused the fetch. So I can't rule out that one of those states the rule.
decides: This settles the 'charge without taking anything off' question in favour of no pick. With a detachable MagSafe wallet (ESR Geo, Apple FineWoven, Smartish Side Hustle) you take the wallet off. With a MagSafe one-piece wallet case (Mujjo, Bellroy) you take the cards out, per Apple's rule. A one-piece case like the Smartish Wallet Slayer is cable-only. So 'MagSafe compatible' on a card-pocket case buys magnet accessories, not charging with cards in. The pick comes down to which you'd rather do each time you charge: take off a wallet or take out cards. The Mujjo cell can change from 'with cards in, not checked' to 'remove cards to charge (Apple's rule)'. Also, the Mujjo product URL in our table now gives a 301 redirect to troubadourgoods.com, and that page did not load (storecheck got HTTP 404; WebFetch hit too many redirects). The row needs a new link or should come out.

findings.label: Apple: items not to put between iPhone and MagSafe Charger
findings.value: "Don't place credit cards, security badges, passports, or key fobs between your iPhone and MagSafe Charger". Apple says this could damage magnetic strips or RFID chips in those items.
findings.source_title: How to use your MagSafe Charger with iPhone - Apple Support
findings.note: Apple's own support page, read live. The risk named covers RFID chips as well as magnetic strips, which conflicts with our page's line that 'chip bank cards are fine'. That line comes from Apple's separate magnets page, which is about the phone's magnets, not about charging.

findings.label: Apple: wallet-style cases while charging
findings.value: "If you have a case that holds any of these sensitive items, remove them before charging"
findings.source_title: How to use your MagSafe Charger with iPhone - Apple Support
findings.note: This applies to any one-piece case with a card pocket on the back (Mujjo, Bellroy 3 Card, Vena vCommuteX). Wireless charging with cards in is against Apple's guidance, whatever the case maker says about magnets.

findings.label: Wireless charging with the wallet attached
findings.value: Not supported: "No, you must take the wallet off first before charging your phone wirelessly."
findings.note: Maker's FAQ answer to the question 'Can wireless charging be used with the MagSafe wallet?'. It confirms the 'Take it off' cell in our table for the Stand. I did not open the same FAQ for the Boost.
